title: Maximum Sum Subarray of Size K
statement: Return the maximum sum of any contiguous subarray of length exactly `k`.
hints: The first window sum is the sum of the first k elements.
The next window drops nums[i - k] and adds nums[i].
Track the maximum window sum as you slide.

approaches.name: Recompute each window
approaches.explanation: Sum every slice of length k.

approaches.name: Fixed sliding window
approaches.explanation: Update the sum in constant time per step.

editorial: A fixed-size window is the simplest sliding-window form. Compute the first sum, then for each new right edge subtract the element that leaves and add the element that enters. The maximum of those sums is the answer. This is also the integer core of the maximum-average problem, since the average is the sum divided by k.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def max_sum_subarray_k(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    window = sum(nums[:k])
    best = window
    for i in range(k, len(nums)):
        window += nums[i] - nums[i - k]
        best = max(best, window)
    return best
